rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion to a narrow, institutionally clarifying application of Arbaugh/Henderson/Hamer that treats § 7703(b)(1)(A) as nonjurisdictional while emphasizing strict, traditional limits on equitable tolling. A separate dissent is likely (most likely by Alito, possibly joined by Thomas) pressing the § 1295(a)(9) structural-linkage/Bowles analogy, with some chance of concurrences from Gorsuch or Barrett to underscore textualism and from Sotomayor/Jackson to highlight access-to-justice concerns.
